root_idea.summary: The evidence records two distinct lexical lines: an anatomical noun and كِينَةٌ meaning a state or condition. It does not securely establish a single broader semantic principle for the root.
root_idea.development: كِينَةٌ is explained as a derivative of كَوْنٌ; the anatomical usage is separately recorded and should not be conflated with that etymological explanation.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Although the Form X group is Quran-attested, the packet supplies only contextual English glosses and a pointer-only Lane entry; no direct Lane or Mufradat evidence establishes a Quranic lexical sense for اِسْتَكَانَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An anatomical part associated with a woman's sexual anatomy; the plural is كُيُونٌ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also recorded as كَيْنَةٌ. The supplied evidence gives the plural form and anatomical association but does not provide a fuller anatomical specification.
In the expression بَاتَ فُلَانٌ بِكِينَةِ سَوْءٍ, it means being in a bad condition or state. This usage is etymologically explained as related to كَوْنٌ.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Pointer-only entry directing the reader to اِسْتَكَنَ under سكن and to كون; it supplies no lexical definition in the packet.
Pointer-only entry directing كَيْنٌ/كَيْنَةٌ to بَظْرٌ; it supplies no independent lexical explanation in the unit text.

cautions: The Quranic Form X occurrences are retained in form accounting but are not given a public Quranic sense because the supplied contextual glosses cannot independently establish lexical meaning and the relevant Lane evidence is cross-reference-only.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: The Quranic occurrences at 3:146:18 and 23:76:5 have contextual glosses “they gave in” and “they submit,” but the packet contains no direct lexical evidence sufficient to determine and document the sense of اِسْتَكَانَ.
